# User guide: Getting started

## In plain words

AI CLI Agents lets you run AI coding assistants inside the Unraid web interface. An assistant is called an agent. The plugin supports Claude Code, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, Kilo Code, Codex CLI, Goose, Qwen Code, Pi Coder, Factory CLI, NanoCoder, Antigravity CLI, Grok Build and Kimi Code. Each agent runs on your server, in a workspace of its own, and it keeps working after you close the browser tab. A workspace is one agent, one folder and one terminal, kept together under one name. This page takes you from the installation to your first working agent.

## Where to find it

The plugin has two places in the Unraid web interface.

- **The AI CLI Agents tab.** It sits in the Unraid top menu. This is the working place. It shows the terminal of your agent. At the left edge it has the drawer (the sliding list of your workspaces). Select **New Workspace** in the drawer to start work.
- **The Settings page.** Open the Unraid **Settings** tab and select **AI CLI Agents**. The address is `/Settings/AICliAgentsManager`. You can also press **Settings** at the bottom of the drawer. The page has six tabs:

| Tab | What you do there |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Configuration** | Choose the Unraid user, the storage places, the terminal look and the behaviour of the plugin. |
| **Agent Store** | Install, upgrade and set up each agent. |
| **Home Storage** | Look after your home (the folder that holds the agent settings, memory and sign-ins) and its backups. |
| **Config Hub** | Keep tools, instructions and skills in step across your agents. |
| **Agent Relay** | Let the workspaces on your server send messages to each other. |
| **Debug Console** | Read the log and collect information for a bug report. |

A small coloured dot with the word **Health** sits at the right end of the tab row. Green means all is well. Amber is a warning. Red needs your attention. Select it to open the Debug Console.

If you cannot find the AI CLI Agents tab, open **Settings, AI CLI Agents, Configuration**. Check that **Show the AI CLI Agents tab** is **Yes**. The choice **No** hides the tab from the top menu. It does not remove the plugin.

## How to use it

### Before you start

- Unraid 7.2 or later.
- An internet connection on the server. The Agent Store downloads each agent when you install it.
- An account or an API key (a secret text that gives access to a service) for the AI service that each agent uses. Each agent has its own sign-in. See the section "Sign in to your agent" below.

### Install the plugin

1. Open the **Apps** tab of Unraid (Community Applications).
2. Search for "AI CLI Agents".
3. Select **Install** and confirm.
4. Expect: Unraid shows the install log. The plugin adds the **AI CLI Agents** tab and the Settings page.

### Install your first agent

You need at least one installed agent before you can start a workspace. If no agent is installed, the AI CLI Agents tab says **No Agents Installed**. Select **Go to Agent Settings**.

1. Open **Settings, AI CLI Agents, Agent Store**.
2. Find the card of the agent you want.
3. Press the install button on the card. It reads **Install** followed by the version number.
4. Expect: a progress bar shows on the card. The card shows the installed version when the install ends.

Each card has chips: **Channel**, **Envs**, **Resources**, **Terminal** and **Args**. The chips stay grey until the agent is installed. The **Envs** chip holds the environment variables and the secrets that the plugin gives to the agent at launch. The guide [Agent Store](agent-store.md) explains every chip.

### The first-run wizard

The first time you open the AI CLI Agents tab, a window called **Welcome to AI CLI Agents** opens. It has three steps. The title bar shows "Step 1 of 3", "Step 2 of 3" or "Step 3 of 3", and dots show where you are.

| Step | Title | What it tells you |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| 1 | **Where does your agent data live?** | The plugin keeps the data of the agents and your home on the flash drive by default. A cache drive gives faster disk access and less wear on the flash drive. If the plugin finds a better place, a box shows **Recommended** with the folder and the free space. If it finds none, the step says that the flash drive is the only available target. |
| 2 | **Copy-Paste in the terminal** | The three ways to copy and paste: the agent copies text for you, the paste icon of the drawer (or the Paste key on a phone) sends your clipboard to the terminal, and Shift plus drag selects text with the browser. |
| 3 | **First-launch authentication** | A list of the installed agents that need a one-time sign-in, each with its icon and a hint. |

Use the buttons at the bottom of the window.

1. Press **Next** to go to the next step. Press **Back** to return.
2. On step 3, press **Finish**.
3. Expect: the window closes. The plugin saves that you finished, and the window does not open again.

**Don't show again** is a small button at the left of the footer. It is on every step. It closes the window and saves the same choice as **Finish**. Select it if you already know the content.

A click outside the window does not close it. You must press **Finish** or **Don't show again**. The window has no button to open it again. All its content is on this page.

On step 1, the link **Agent Settings → Config tab** opens the Settings page on the Configuration tab. The link leaves the wizard unfinished. The wizard opens again the next time you open the AI CLI Agents tab. On a phone the window uses the full width and its buttons are 44 pixels high.

> [!NOTE]
> Step 2 names the paste controls that exist now. Paste is the clipboard icon on the drawer tab (or in the icon row of a pinned drawer). The page has no Mouse toggle. The mouse behaviour of tmux (the session manager that keeps a terminal alive on the server) is the option **Mouse mode** in the **tmux** tab of **Session settings**. The guide [The terminal](terminal.md) explains copy and paste in full.

### Start your first workspace

1. Open the AI CLI Agents tab.
2. Open the drawer. Press the tab at the left edge of the page.
3. Press **New Workspace**.
4. Select an agent by its icon and name.
5. Type or browse to a folder. The picker starts in the folder set as **Starting folder** (`/mnt/user` by default).
6. Press **Start New**. If the agent has a saved conversation for the folder, the button **Resume** is also there.
7. Expect: a row for the workspace appears in the drawer. The page shows "Starting" and the name of the agent. Then the terminal of the agent opens.

The guide [Workspaces](workspaces.md) explains the picker and the drawer in full.

### Sign in to your agent

Each agent needs a sign-in the first time you use it. You do it inside the terminal of the workspace. You do it once for each agent. The plugin saves the sign-in in your home. It stays after a reboot and after an upgrade of the plugin or the agent.

| Agent | First sign-in |
| :-- | :-- |
| Claude Code | Type `/login` in the terminal on the first launch. |
| Gemini CLI | Run `gemini auth login`. It signs in with your Google account. |
| Codex CLI | Run `codex login` (a browser sign-in). Or add your `OPENAI_API_KEY` in the **Envs** chip of the Agent Store card. The key needs no interactive sign-in. On Unraid, Codex runs without an operating-system sandbox, and an approval step gates its commands. |
| Antigravity CLI | On the first launch the agent prints a Google authorisation link. Open it in a browser, approve the access and paste the code into the terminal. |
| Grok Build | Follow the account-linking steps that the agent shows on the first launch. As an option, add `XAI_API_KEY` in the **Envs** chip. |
| Kimi Code | The agent may already know your account. If it asks you to sign in, use the login choice inside the agent. |

The other agents show no hint in the wizard. These are OpenCode, Kilo Code, Pi Coder, GitHub Copilot, Factory CLI, NanoCoder, Goose and Qwen Code. Read the documentation of each agent for its sign-in. Most of them read an API key from an environment variable. Add such a key in the **Envs** chip of the agent card. The Secrets section of that chip hides the value and does not show it again after you save it.

To add a key for one workspace only, open the row menu of the workspace and select **Session settings**. See [Workspace settings and automation](workspace-settings-and-automation.md).

## Choices and settings

These settings matter most on the first day. The full list is in [Settings reference](settings-reference.md).

| Setting | What it does | Default | When to change it |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Show the AI CLI Agents tab** (Configuration) | Shows or hides the AI CLI Agents tab in the top menu. | Yes | Choose No only if you want to use the plugin through the Settings page. |
| **Home Storage** (Configuration, **Change…**) | The place where your home is saved. | The flash drive | Move it to a cache pool for speed and less flash wear. |
| **Agent Storage** (Configuration, **Change…**) | The place where the installed agents are saved. | The flash drive | Move it to a cache pool when you install many agents. |
| **Starting folder** (Configuration) | The folder where the folder picker starts when no other folder applies. | `/mnt/user` | Set it to the folder that holds your projects. |
| **Terminal user** (Configuration) | The Unraid user that runs the terminals. It decides whose home you see. | `root` | Change it only if you want the agents to run as another user. |
| **Colour scheme** and **Text size** (Configuration) | The colours and the text size of the terminal. | Dark, 14 px | Change them for your eyes or your screen. |

A change on the Configuration tab saves at once. Moving **Home Storage** or **Agent Storage** shows a warning first and then moves the data. See [Home and agent storage](storage.md).

## Where the plugin keeps your data

| What | Where | Kept after a reboot? |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| The plugin settings | On the flash drive, in the folder `/boot/config/plugins/unraid-aicliagents/`. | Yes |
| Your home: agent settings, memory, sign-ins, the list of workspaces, the saved conversation of each workspace and the settings of each workspace | In the place you chose as **Home Storage**. | Yes |
| The installed agents | In the place you chose as **Agent Storage**. | Yes |
| The working copy of your home while you work | In RAM, in the folder `/tmp/unraid-aicliagents/`. | No. The plugin saves it to Home Storage first. |
| The log | In RAM, in the same folder. The **Debug Console** tab shows it. | No |
| Choices that belong to one browser: the pinned drawer, the place of the drawer tab, the folder picker choices (hidden folders, sort order, open Favourites), the device label | In that browser. | Until you clear the data of the browser. |

The plugin saves your home to Home Storage in the background. **Save unsaved home changes every** on the Configuration tab sets how often (every 2 hours by default). The **Save now** button next to it saves at once. A save is not the same as a backup. For a second copy, see [Home backup and restore](backup-restore.md).

## What happens behind the scenes

Each workspace runs a tmux session on the server. The browser terminal attaches to that session. When you close the browser tab, the session and the agent keep running. The plugin keeps your home and the agents on compressed read-only layers with a fast write layer on top, so the flash drive does not wear out. See C4 Component: Session Process Management and C4 Component: Storage Management.

## If something goes wrong

| What you see | What it means | What to do |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| The wizard did not open | You finished it before, or the page has not loaded its settings. | Nothing is lost. The wizard has no reopen button. Use this page. |
| **No Agents Installed** | No agent is installed. | Press **Go to Agent Settings**. Install an agent in the Agent Store. |
| The drawer button reads **Emergency Session** | Your home or agent storage is not available. For example, the array is stopped and the storage is on the array. | Read [Home and agent storage](storage.md). |
| A card **Storage Unavailable** after a reboot | The folder of the workspace is not mounted yet. | Wait. The page tries again every 10 seconds, and the terminal opens when the folder is there. |
| The agent asks you to sign in again | The sign-in is missing or has expired. | Repeat the sign-in command in the terminal. |
| A red or amber **Health** dot | The plugin found a problem. | Select the dot. See [Health, Activity and troubleshooting](health-and-troubleshooting.md). |
